name: Brewfather
tagline: Recipe design, batch tracking and fermentation logging for homebrewers, with cloud sync and brew device integrations.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The math is the easy part: ABV, Tinseth IBU, SRM, mash and sparge volumes, efficiency, water salt additions are all published formulas an agent can implement correctly in a session. A local recipe designer with a batch log and BeerXML import/export is genuinely a weekend build, and for a solo brewer who already knows their system it covers most brew days. The gaps are the parts that make Brewfather pleasant: a real mobile app you can poke with wet hands in the garage, sync between phone and laptop, and live hydrometer integrations with Tilt, iSpindel and friends. You also inherit the chore of sourcing a decent malt, hop and yeast database instead of getting one maintained for you. Buildable, but you will be maintaining a hobby inside a hobby.
coreLoopDIY: A local-first recipe designer and batch log that computes gravity, IBU, color and water volumes from your ingredients and equipment profile, with BeerXML in and out.
requirements: An ingredient dataset: scrape or hand-enter malts, hops and yeast, or import from BeerXML files you already have
Your own equipment profile numbers: boil-off rate, mash tun deadspace, efficiency
Optional: a BLE-capable device if you want to read a Tilt yourself
whatYouLose: Native iOS and Android apps built for a brewery floor, not a browser tab
Sync across devices, plus backups you do not have to think about
Plug and play hardware integrations: Tilt, iSpindel, Plaato, Grainfather, RAPT
A curated and updated ingredient library with real hop alpha ranges and yeast attenuation data
Shared and community recipes you can fork instead of typing in from scratch
moatNotes: The ingredient and style database plus years of device partnerships are the actual product; the calculators are textbook.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the subscription is cheap relative to a single grain bill and it removes every annoyance on brew day. You get the phone in your pocket, the fermentation chart updating itself from a floating sensor, the ingredient list that already knows what Citra typically runs at, and a backup of nine years of batches that survives your laptop dying. Homebrewers are already spending money and time on the beer; very few want to also debug their own IndexedDB schema at 6am while the mash sits at 66C.
notes: The brewing math is open knowledge and always has been; the convenience is what you are renting.
prompt:
Build a local-first homebrewing recipe designer and batch log. No accounts, no server, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript, Tailwind for styling, Dexie (IndexedDB) for storage, Recharts for charts. Everything runs in the browser from `npm run dev`. No backend.

Data model: Fermentable (name, type, color in Lovibond, potential/PPG, max percent), Hop (name, alpha acid, form), Yeast (name, lab, attenuation, min/max temp), EquipmentProfile (batch size, boil time, boil off rate per hour, mash tun deadspace, trub loss, brewhouse efficiency), Recipe (name, style, target batch size, fermentable additions, hop additions with time and use, yeast, mash steps, notes), Batch (linked recipe, brew date, measured gravities, fermentation readings, tasting notes, status).

Calculations, implement and unit test these with Vitest:
- Original and final gravity from fermentables, efficiency and batch size
- ABV, both the simple and the Cutaiar-style corrected formula, show the corrected one
- IBU via Tinseth, with boil gravity correction, supporting boil, whirlpool and dry hop (dry hop contributes zero IBU)
- Color via Morey from MCU, render as a swatch
- Strike water temperature, mash water and sparge water volumes, pre boil volume from boil off
- Apparent attenuation from measured OG and FG

UI: four screens, Recipes, Batches, Ingredients, Equipment. Recipe editor recalculates every number live as you type and shows OG, FG, ABV, IBU, SRM, BU:GU against editable style ranges. Batch view has a fermentation log table where you add date, gravity and temperature readings by hand, charted over time.

Import and export: parse and emit BeerXML 1.0 for recipes, plus a full JSON dump and restore of the whole Dexie database. Seed the ingredient tables from a `seed/ingredients.json` file I can replace; ship maybe 40 fermentables, 30 hops and 15 yeasts as plausible starter data and clearly mark it as unverified placeholder data in the UI.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, cloud sync, mobile apps, Bluetooth or Tilt or iSpindel integrations, water chemistry salt solver, inventory and shopping lists.

Deliverables: working app, passing tests for every formula above, and a README documenting each formula with its source name so I can check the math myself.
